## Problem

When a new project is created (or an existing one initialized) with an AGENTS.md, the current installer/template behavior emits the full duplicated instruction set as a local file. This is how the four sibling projects ended up with large local AGENTS.md files that duplicate the global one (see SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N).

## User story

As a developer creating a new project, I want the AGENTS.md installer to emit only the canonical global-reference structure so new projects never start by duplicating the global rules.

## Desired change

Improve the tooling/template that creates AGENTS.md for a project so the generated local file contains only the canonical structure (as adopted by SorraAgents itself in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W):

    ## Global agent guidance

    Read the global agent instructions at ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md — they define the core principles, the Worklog (wl) work-item workflow, and the coding disciplines that apply to every project.

    ## Project-specific guidance

    (project-specific rules are added by the project owner here, never by copying the global file)

- Locate the installer/template mechanism (search scripts, wl/pi project init, templates dir, .pi scaffolding) and change the emitted template.
- The canonical structure is emitted by default; project-specific rules are added by the project owner on top, never by copying the global file.
- If the installer supports an option to copy the global file (e.g. for offline/standalone use), keep it as an explicit opt-in.
- Coordinate with the Worklog side: ContextHub wl init should delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install rather than duplicating it (tracked in ContextHub work item WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The installer/template that creates AGENTS.md now emits exactly the canonical structure above (## Global agent guidance reference + ## Project-specific guidance placeholder).
2. Creating a fresh project (or re-running init) produces an AGENTS.md whose content is the canonical structure, not a copy of the global file.
3. Existing behavior for projects with custom local rules is unaffected (they keep their local rules below the reference line).
4. Any docs describing the installer and the global-vs-project AGENTS.md split are updated.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- TBD at plan time: search for AGENTS.md templates/installers (e.g. ~/.pi/agent/ scaffolding, pi init, project setup scripts). Candidate locations: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/ (pi's own project init), any templates/ dirs in ~/.pi/agent/.

- related-to:SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G (SorraAgents AGENTS.md dedup)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N (sibling projects AGENTS.md dedup)

This work standardizes the end-of-session report into a single, quickly scannable format produced by a shared helper skill that other skills call.

## Users

- **Producers/operators** who review the end of every skill session and need to quickly scan: what was done, are acceptance criteria met, what state is the work item in, what actions (if any) are required of them.
- **Agents/skills** that need a canonical, reusable report template with deterministic metadata (avoiding each skill inventing its own format).

### User stories

- As a producer, I want every skill session to end with the same report structure, so I can scan results quickly without re-reading raw session output.
- As a skill author, I want a helper skill that provides the canonical report template and metadata (type, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, children, audit), so my skill produces compliant reports with minimal effort.
- As a producer, I want to see the acceptance criteria with per-criterion met/unmet verdicts, so I can tell at a glance whether the work item is ready.
- As a producer, I want an explicit "Producer Actions" section, so I know exactly what (if anything) I need to do next.
- As a producer, I want a freeform Notes section, so the agent can surface context, caveats, or assumptions that don't fit the structured sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new helper skill (e.g., `skill/report/` or `skill/session-report/`) exists with a SKILL.md defining the canonical end-of-session report format exactly as specified: header `# Completed <skill_name>`, work-item title + id, headline summary, `## Acceptance Criteria` table, `## Meta-Data`, `## Producer Actions`, `## Notes`, `## Conclusion`.
- [ ] The report template matches the requested layout: AC rows are `|<ac#>|<Description>|<Metric>|<met|unmet>|`; Meta-Data lists Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit each as `<icon> <text>`; Producer Actions defaults to `None needed`; Notes is freeform; Conclusion states `<This completes the <skill_name> process for <id> (<title>). Ready for <next_action>.`
- [ ] The report includes the `## Notes` section between `## Producer Actions` and `## Conclusion` for freeform agent commentary.
- [ ] Meta-Data values (Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit) are populated deterministically from the work item (via `wl show <id> --json`), so the report reflects the current worklog state rather than the agent's memory.
- [ ] **Icon mappings match the canonical ContextHub set** (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`, the set used by the `wl` CLI itself): priority 🚨/⭐/📋/🐢, status 🔓/🔄/✔️/⛔/🗑️/💬, stage 💡/📥/📋/🛠️/🔍/🏁, risk 🌱/⚠️/🔥/🚨, effort 🐜/🐇/🐕/🐘/🐋, audit ✅/❌/❔, with bracketed text fallbacks (`[CRIT]`, `[OPEN]`, `[IDEA]`, `[LOW]`, `[XS]`, `[YES]`, etc.) when icons are unavailable. The helper documents the full mapping table and its ContextHub source so the sets cannot drift. (ContextHub already provides this shared helper — `src/icons.ts` + `docs/icons-design.md` — so no new ContextHub work item is required; see Related work.)
- [ ] The helper skill documents a clear invocation contract (how another skill calls it at the end of its session — e.g., a short embeddable instruction block) that skills embed as their final step.
- [ ] **All existing skills that work on work-items are wired to invoke the helper** at the end of their session, each with its SKILL.md updated to reference the helper: intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, and author-command (any skill whose flow creates/updates work items). Verification: grep across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows every work-item skill ends with the standardized report instruction.
- [ ] A test validates the report renderer: given a work item + AC verdicts, it produces the expected report structure (sections present, AC table rows, metadata icons/values, defaults for empty fields).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including the new skill's SKILL.md, README, and any references in migrated skills.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The helper skill is invoked by other skills; it does not replace a skill's own workflow or status lifecycle management.
- The report is produced at the end of a skill session; it should not require new work-item state changes beyond what the calling skill already performs.
- Report must remain scannable: prose sections (headline, Notes) are concise; structured sections carry the details.
- Keep it simple: a single template + metadata renderer (script or documented wl command) is sufficient; no orchestration framework.
- Icon mappings are sourced from ContextHub's canonical set — do not invent new icons in individual skills.

## Existing state

- Skills currently end sessions with ad-hoc summaries: e.g., implement closes with `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary> / Work committed to dev`; intake ends with an Objective/AC/Effort-Risk summary; audit has its own persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`).
- No shared report template or helper skill exists (`grep` for `## Producer Actions` / `## Meta-Data` / `## Conclusion` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` returns nothing).
- Worklog exposes all needed metadata via `wl show <id> --json` (issueType, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, childCount, auditResult/audit status).
- Effort/risk use t-shirt sizes (XS–XL) from `skill/effort-and-risk/references/t-shirt_sizes.json`; risk levels are low/medium/high.
- **ContextHub already provides the canonical icon set**: `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` (spec) and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (TypeScript implementation), consumed by the `wl` CLI (`dist/icons.js`). Mappings cover priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, and producer-review flags, each with emoji + bracketed text fallback + accessible label.
- Skills live in `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/report/SKILL.md` (or `skill/session-report/`) defining:
   - The canonical report template (exact section order and layout as specified, including `## Notes` before `## Conclusion`).
   - Icon mappings per Meta-Data field sourced from ContextHub's canonical set (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`), with bracketed text fallbacks.
   - Instructions for populating each section (AC verdicts from the calling skill's own evaluation; Meta-Data from `wl show --json`).
   - A short "how to invoke" contract that other skills embed (e.g., a call-out block to add to a skill's final step).
2. Provide `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (or a documented `wl show` + template recipe) that renders the Meta-Data block deterministically from `wl show <id> --json` — helpers to extract/format metadata, icons (reusing ContextHub mappings), and defaults.
3. Wire the helper into **all** work-item skills: update each `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) so the final step invokes the standardized report.
4. Add tests (e.g., `skill/report/tests/`) validating the template and metadata rendering.
5. Add an example rendered report in the SKILL.md so agents can copy the pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — new helper skill defining the canonical report format, ContextHub-sourced icon mappings, and invocation contract.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — metadata renderer reading `wl show --json`, reusing ContextHub icon mappings.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — tests for template structure, metadata icons, defaults.
- `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` for every work-item skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) — final step invokes the helper report.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — its existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, AC status table) is the closest precedent; reconcile its end-of-session summary with the new template.

## Related work

- `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` + `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` — **canonical icon set** (priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, producer-review) with emoji + text fallbacks + accessible labels; consumed by the `wl` CLI. The report skill reuses these mappings. (This is the shared helper the requirement asks for — no new ContextHub work item needed.)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table, `## Variance Decisions`, `## Children Status`); the closest existing structured-report precedent to reconcile/align with.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — defines risk (low/medium/high) and effort t-shirt (XS–XL) values used in the Meta-Data section.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — example helper skill with scripts + tests + a "compact report" pattern.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — skills' shared status/stage transitions; the report's Status/Stage metadata reflects these.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** wiring the helper into every work-item skill is broad; the requirement is explicit, so all work-item skills are in scope for this item. Skills that do not touch work items (e.g., speak) are excluded.
- **Icon consistency:** icon mappings must come from the ContextHub canonical set (single source of truth) to avoid per-skill divergence; the helper documents the mapping table + source. Unknown values fall back to a neutral marker; icons are decorative — the textual value always accompanies them, so reports remain readable in non-emoji terminals/views.
- **Metadata drift:** report reflects the worklog at render time; if the calling skill changes state after rendering, the report may be stale. Mitigation: render the report as the final step of the session.
- **Audit reconciliation:** audit's existing persisted format differs (it is machine-verified). Its end-of-session summary is reconciled with the template; its persisted machine-verified report format is preserved.
- **Assumption:** Meta-Data is rendered deterministically from worklog where possible; the agent supplies only prose (headline, Notes, Producer Actions, Conclusion next-action).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which skill should be the first adopter / what is the migration scope?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Add an AC that wires the helper into all existing skills that work on work-items." The migration scope is therefore ALL work-item skills, not just 1–2 adopters. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What icon mappings should be used?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Icon mappings should be the same as those used in ../ContextHub. If that project does not have a shared helper you can use then create a work item in that project to do so and make this work item dependent upon it." Research: ContextHub provides the canonical icon set in `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (consumed by the `wl` CLI), covering all Meta-Data fields. No new ContextHub work item is required — the helper references that set. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "Should the report be persisted (e.g., work-item comment) or stdout only?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: stdout only for v1; persistence as follow-up). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should Meta-Data be auto-generated from `wl show --json`?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: yes, via a small renderer script). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).

## Summary

The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) crashes with an unhandled `TypeError` in `_map_gaps_to_children` (line ~2930) when a Phase 2 deep-analysis AC result carries `evidence` as a `dict` instead of a string:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "audit_runner.py", line 5343, in <module>
    raise SystemExit(main())
  ...
  File "audit_runner.py", line 2930, in _map_gaps_to_children
    for m in re.finditer(r"([\w./-]+\.\w+)(?::\d+)?", evidence):
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'dict'
```

`_map_gaps_to_children` does `evidence = r.get("evidence", "") or ""` — a truthy dict passes through unvalidated into `re.finditer`, which requires str/bytes. ## Summary

**Bug (stale-audit correctness gap).** `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 696) fingerprints only: git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files list. However, the audit's own file-scope manifest reads `git status --porcelain` (untracked/modified files) and the deep-analysis model reads the **working tree**, not just HEAD. So uncommitted code changes between audits do **not** invalidate freshness — the freshness gate can serve a stale audit for code that has since changed.

The docs claim "a change in ANY fingerprint component invalidates freshness", but working-tree state is not a component.

## Expected behaviour

Include the working-tree state in the fingerprint payload: a hash of `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` output (sorted, deterministic). A change in any uncommitted file, untracked file, or commit invalidates freshness; an untouched repo keeps the same fingerprint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modifying an uncommitted tracked file invalidates the fingerprint (stale audit → re-run).
2. Adding an untracked file invalidates the fingerprint.
3. Committing a change also invalidates (via the existing HEAD sha component).
4. An untouched working tree + unchanged description + unchanged Key Files keeps the same fingerprint (freshness preserved).
5. Unit tests cover all four cases; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.

# Intake Brief: Plan/intake skills iterate over children & verify AC coverage

## Problem statement

When the `plan` or `intake` skills run on a work item that has child work items,
they currently process only the target item — they never descend into the
children. This leaves parent/child AC coverage unverified: a parent's acceptance
criteria may not be collectively covered by its children's ACs, and children are
never themselves planned/intaked (so the decomposition tree can be incomplete
or inconsistent at depth).

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:plan`** on an epic or other parent with children —
  need the skill to recurse over the whole tree so every level is planned, and
  to verify that the union of child ACs covers the parent ACs.
- **Agents running `/skill:intake`** on a parent with children — need intake to
  run per child (when children exist) and to verify cross-level AC coverage.
- **Operators** — get decomposition trees whose ACs are guaranteed (or
  explicitly flagged) to cover their parents, with gaps auto-closed where
  resolvable and hard conflicts surfaced instead of silently passing.

Example user stories:

- As an agent planning an epic with children, I want the plan skill to iterate
  the whole subtree (respecting dependency order) so I don't have to invoke
  `/skill:plan` per child manually.
- As an agent planning a parent, I want a final review step that verifies the
  children's ACs collectively cover the parent's ACs, auto-closing gaps it can
  resolve and stopping with a clear report when it cannot, so a `plan_complete`
  stage is only reached when coverage is guaranteed.
- As an operator re-running intake on a decomposed epic, I want intake to verify
  AC coverage across the existing children (and per child when configured) so
  the tree stays coherent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tree iteration — plan):** Running `/skill:plan` on a work item with
  children processes the entire subtree, not just the target: the skill
  iterates children (each child's own plan run, recursing to any depth), in
  dependency order first (`wl dep` edges), then listed order. Verified by a
  test with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting
  every node is planned and the processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2 (tree iteration — intake):** Running `/skill:intake` on a work item
  with children runs intake per child (recursing the subtree) and also verifies
  AC coverage across existing children. Verified by a test where intake on a
  parent with children runs per child and reports coverage.
- **AC3 (collective coverage):** After processing, for every parent node in the
  tree, the union of its children's acceptance criteria collectively covers the
  parent's acceptance criteria (each parent AC is covered by at least one child
  AC). Verified by a coverage-check test with a parent whose ACs are covered
  by children and a negative test where coverage is missing.
- **AC4 (final review step — auto-close & stop):** The skills' final review
  step closes coverage gaps it can resolve unambiguously (e.g. adding a missing
  child AC that directly maps to an uncovered parent AC), and when a gap or
  conflict cannot be resolved, stops and reports rather than advancing
  (`plan_complete`/`intake_complete` not set; item left `open` with a comment
  describing the conflict). Verified by tests: one where an unambiguous gap is
  auto-closed, one where an unresolvable conflict prevents stage advancement.
- **AC5 (docs & tests):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes (plan SKILL.md, intake SKILL.md, shared helper docstrings), and the
  full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Worklog API only:** read children via `wl show <id> --children --json`;
  dependency edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`. No direct worklog file edits.
- **No work item for the process itself:** the skills must not create a work
  item to track the iteration itself.
- **Idempotence:** re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate
  comments; existing children are reused/updated per the existing plan-skill
  idempotence rules.
- **Status lifecycle:** all status transitions go through `StatusLifecycle`
  (intake via `intake.py`, plan via `StatusLifecycle.update_status`); the new
  final review step must leave the item in a valid terminal status (`open`,
  `blocked`, or `completed`) even when it stops on an unresolvable conflict.
- **Conservative auto-closing:** only close gaps that are unambiguous (a child
  AC that clearly maps to an uncovered parent AC). Never invent requirements —
  if intent is unclear, record an Open Question / stop instead.
- **Scope:** affects the `plan` and `intake` skills (SKILL.md workflows) and
  their shared helpers. Must not change audit, implement, or other skills'
  behavior. Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` decomposes the target into child feature work items;
  it creates children (Process step 7) and runs six automated review stages on
  the freshly generated feature plan, but never recurses into children and has
  no AC-coverage check across the tree. Its "Automated review on existing
  content" path (skip decision) reviews existing content but still does not
  iterate the tree.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` prepares a single work item (claim → gather → draft →
  five mini-reviews → find-related → finish). It has no child iteration or
  coverage verification.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` provides shared autoplan/approval-gate logic;
  it has no tree/coverage helpers.
- `wl` supports `wl show <id> --children --json` and `wl dep list/add/rm`, so
  tree traversal and ordering data are available without new CLI work.
- The audit skill already has parent/child awareness (child stage checks,
  inherited passes) — a useful reference for tree semantics but NOT to be
  modified by this item.

## Desired change

- **Shared helper (new or extended):** a module (e.g.
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` or new functions in `plan_helpers.py`) that:
  1. Fetches the full descendant tree via `wl show <id> --children --json`.
  2. Orders siblings by `wl dep` edges (topological) then listed order.
  3. Extracts ACs from each item's description (`## Acceptance Criteria`
     section).
  4. Computes coverage: for each parent AC, whether any child AC covers it.
  5. Auto-closes unambiguous gaps; returns an explicit list of unresolvable
     conflicts.
- **Plan skill:** add a "tree iteration" step (before/around Process step 7)
  that recurses into children; add a final "AC coverage review" step after the
  six review stages that applies the helper, auto-closes gaps, and on
  unresolvable conflicts stops without advancing the stage (leaving the item
  `open` with a conflict comment).
- **Intake skill:** add a per-child intake pass (when children exist) and a
  final AC-coverage verification step mirroring the plan behavior.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the shared helper (tree fetch/order, AC extraction,
  coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection) plus skill-workflow
  tests asserting stage advancement is blocked on unresolvable conflicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add tree-iteration and final AC-coverage review steps
  to the Process section.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add per-child intake pass and AC-coverage
  verification step.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (new) — Shared tree traversal, ordering,
  AC extraction, coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection
  (or equivalent functions added to `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` if shared
  placement is not preferred).
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Extend with tree/coverage helper
  tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`).
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Workflow tests for per-child intake and coverage
  stop/advance behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency fix; documents the
  audit skill's child-stage semantics (children in `in_review` don't block
  parent closure). Reference only; not to be modified here.
- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce wall-clock time; example of a
  parent item decomposed into children via the plan skill.
- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — Reduce initial LLM context; an epic with 6 children,
  useful as a real-world tree for manual validation of the new iteration.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Already has child-aware logic (recursive child
  implementations, terminal-stage checks); a pattern reference for how skills
  handle trees.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Parent/child
  verdict and stage semantics; reference for tree behavior conventions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: recursion depth/time.** Deep trees could make plan/intake slow or
  loop. Mitigation: recursion bounded by the actual tree; each child processed
  once; idempotent re-runs. Note: no explicit depth cap is assumed unless
  needed — flag in implementation if cycles are possible in worklog trees.
- **Risk: AC extraction brittleness.** Descriptions vary in formatting; ACs may
  be missing or malformed. Mitigation: tolerant extraction; missing ACs treated
  as an uncovered gap reported to the user rather than silently ignored.
- **Risk: auto-closing gaps could invent content.** Mitigation: only
  unambiguous, directly-mapped gaps are auto-closed; everything else stops with
  a report (per AC4).
- **Assumption:** worklog trees are acyclic (a work item's children cannot
  contain it). If a cycle is ever detected, the skill stops and reports.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list <id> --json` output shape is stable; the helper
  parses both object and array JSON shapes (per existing plan skill guidance).
- **Scope-creep note:** any additional "verify child ACs against parent at
  audit time" ideas are out of scope for this item (audit behavior unchanged)
  and would be tracked as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the iteration recurse through the entire tree (a parent with
  children whose children also have children — plan/intake each level), or just
  one level of direct children?" — Answer (user): "entire tree". Final: entire
  tree, any depth.
- Q2: "Does 'run the skill on each dependently' mean respecting the `wl dep`
  dependency edges (topological order — an item only after its prerequisites)?
  Or just sequential order as listed?" — Answer (user): "respect dependencies,
  then order listed". Final: topological order by `wl dep` edges, ties broken
  by listed order.
- Q3: "When the final review finds parent ACs not covered by child ACs, should
  the skill block completion (refuse to advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`
  until fixed or explicitly waived), or report the gaps and continue?" — Answer
  (user): "it should close the gaps. If there is conflict that cannot be
  resolved then stop and report, refusing to advance". Final: auto-close
  unambiguous gaps; unresolvable conflicts stop the skill, item left `open`
  with a report comment, stage not advanced.
- Q4: "When intake runs on a parent with children (e.g. re-running on a
  decomposed epic), should it: (a) run intake per child, (b) only verify AC
  coverage across existing children, or (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both".
  Final: intake runs per child AND verifies coverage across existing children.

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

# All skills emit `</end_session>` marker on terminal state

## Problem statement

Skills currently end sessions with inconsistent closing text — some print `<work-item-id>: <summary>`, others say "This completes the <skill> process for <id>", and others produce varied output. A standardized `</end_session>` marker at the very end of every terminal skill session would make it easy for both humans and automation to detect session completion.

## Users

- **Operators (producers)** scanning session output who need a reliable visual cue that a skill has finished without pending questions.
- **Automation loops** (e.g., Ralph) that invoke skills programmatically and need a deterministic signal to detect when a skill has reached a terminal state.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to see `</end_session>` as the last line of every skill session, so I can instantly know the skill has completed.
- As an automation system, I want to grep for `</end_session>` in a skill's output to reliably detect completion, so I don't have to parse unpredictable closing text.
- As a skill author, I want a single sentence to add as my skill's final step, so I don't have to invent my own closing convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single sentence is added as the final step to **every** work-item workflow skill in `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) instructing the agent to end its terminal output with `</end_session>`.
- [ ] The `</end_session>` marker is **not** added to helper-only skills that don't have their own session lifecycle (e.g., `speak`).
- [ ] The marker is emitted **only** when the skill reaches a terminal state without open questions for the operator — question-ended sessions (where the agent is asking for clarification) do not output the marker.
- [ ] The standardized report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ) includes `</end_session>` as its final output line when producing a report, since it is invoked by the work-item skills.
- [ ] The existing closing conventions (e.g., implement's `<work-item-id>: <summary> / Work committed to dev`, intake's "This completes the Intake process…") are preserved **before** `</end_session>` — the marker is appended, not a replacement.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** Only work-item workflow skills listed above (not helpers like `speak`, not `command/` prompts, not the main agent loop).
- **Marker format:** Exactly `</end_session>` on its own line, as the final line of the final agent message.
- **Preserve existing output:** Skills still output their normal summary/AC/Effort-Risk content; `</end_session>` is an additional terminator, not a replacement.
- **Question-ended sessions:** If a skill session ends with unanswered questions for the operator, `</end_session>` is **not** emitted.

## Existing state

- Skills end sessions with ad-hoc closing text:
  - `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: "Close your response with: `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary>

Work committed to dev`"
  - `skill/intake/SKILL.md`: "Finish with 'This completes the Intake process for <work-item-id> <work-item-title>'"
  - `skill/plan/SKILL.md`: "End with: 'This completes the Plan process for <work-item-id>'"
- No skill currently outputs `</end_session>`.
- Related item SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S (standardize report format) is in `plan_complete` stage with 4 children; this intake is folded into that item's scope (per operator decision).

## Desired change

Add one instruction line to each work-item skill's SKILL.md final step: "End with `</end_session>`" (or equivalent phrasing that fits the skill's closing style). The `</end_session>` marker is appended after whatever closing summary the skill already produces.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to finishing step
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to final report output
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/git-management/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/owner-inference/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step

## Related work

- **Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S)** — open / plan_complete / feature. This intake is folded into that item. Children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ. The report helper skill's children are in scope for adding `</end_session>` to their final outputs.

The children share this parent work item so coordination is internal to SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S.
- **Question-ended sessions:** Agents may occasionally forget to skip `</end_session>` when a question is pending. This is a soft risk — the marker is cosmetic; the real signal is workflow state.
- **Assumption:** The report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children) will be wired into all work-item skills and should also emit `</end_session>` when it produces a report.
- **Assumption:** `speak` is the only helper-only skill excluded (no session lifecycle). If other helpers exist without sessions, they are also excluded.

Excludes helpers like `speak`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Exact format & consumer?" — Answer (operator): "Exactly `</end_session>`, consumed by both humans and automation, only emitted on terminal state (no open questions)." Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief: Enable git submodules in implement worktrees (implement.py start) (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ)

## Problem statement

When `implement.py start` creates a git worktree, submodules inside the worktree are not initialized. The submodule directories are empty, causing builds and tests that depend on submodule content to fail silently or with confusing errors. This was observed in SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N where a test failure was traced to an uninitialized submodule in a worktree.

## Users

- AI agents running `/skill:implement <id>` on repos that use git submodules.
- Human developers running `python3 implement.py start <id>` directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `implement.py start` runs `git submodule update --init --recursive` in the new worktree after worktree creation succeeds.
- AC2: If `git submodule update --init --recursive` fails, `implement.py start` logs a warning (via `LOG.warning`) but does **not** abort — start continues and the worktree is usable.
- AC3: A dedicated helper function (e.g. `_ensure_submodules(worktree_path, repo_root)`) is extracted at call site, following the same pattern as the existing `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()` helper.
- AC4: Unit tests cover: (a) submodules are initialized on a fresh worktree, (b) submodule initialization failure does not abort start, (c) repos without submodules are unaffected.
- AC5: `implement/SKILL.md` documents the submodule behavior (that submodules are auto-initialized and that failures produce a warning).
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Best-effort only: submodule initialization failure is never fatal.
- Must not change the existing node_modules symlink helper (no interference).
- Must follow the existing call-site pattern: helper function defined before `start()` main flow, invoked after `git_worktree_add` succeeds and after node_modules symlink (line 1209).
- Must not add external dependencies.

## Existing state

- `implement.py start` creates the worktree via `git_worktree_add()` (line ~402), then auto-symlinks `node_modules` (line ~1209) via `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()`. Submodules are never touched.
- `git worktree add` does **not** automatically initialize submodules in the new worktree — `--recurse-submodules` was added to `git worktree add` in Git 2.42 (we use 2.53.0), but `implement.py start` does not use it.
- Real-world evidence: a comment in SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N records `"initial single failure was uninitialized submodule in worktree; resolved with git..."` — the same pattern that caused the node_modules issue (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B).

## Desired change

After `git_worktree_add()` succeeds and after the node_modules symlink call, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` in the worktree via a best-effort helper that catches failures and logs a warning.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add `_ensure_submodules()` helper (~50 lines, parallel to `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`), invoke at call site after line ~1209.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document submodule auto-initialization behavior.
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` — pattern reference for test structure (mocked git commands, tmp repo setup, subprocess harness).
- New: `tests/test_implement_submodules.py` — unit tests for the submodule helper.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Authentication failures:** Private submodules may fail if no credentials are available in the worktree. Mitigated by best-effort (warning-only). The worktree remains usable.
- **Performance on large submodule trees:** `--recursive` can be slow for repos with many nested submodules. Acceptable — this is expected git behavior; no timeout change needed.

**Summary:** The audit freshness gate (skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`) keys freshness on the whole-repo git HEAD sha. ANY commit to the repo — even one touching files unrelated to the work item — changes HEAD, invalidates the content fingerprint, and forces a full two-phase re-audit. This caused a real false re-audit: NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U was audited "Ready to close: No" (AC5 partial), the content fingerprint was byte-identical on re-audit, yet an operator `/skill:audit` invocation re-ran the full pipeline (twice, dry-run and persisted), and the final persisted verdict flipped to "Ready to close: Yes" purely from model judgment variance on the same unverifiable AC — no new evidence. A freshness gate that actually asserted "the work is in HEAD" would have returned the stored verdict.

**Desired behavior:** freshness must be decided per work item, not per repo. If NO file touched by the work item has changed since the work was committed, the stored audit verdict stands — no re-audit, no model calls. If any touched file changed, the audit is stale and re-runs.

**User stories:**
- As an operator running `/skill:audit <id>` on an item whose work files are unchanged, I want the stored verdict returned in seconds so unrelated repo commits never trigger an expensive re-audit.
- As an operator, I want the gate to be strict about the work item itself: any change to files the item touched (or to its ACs/description/Key Files) must invalidate freshness.

**How to determine "files touched by the work item":**
1. Commits referencing the work item ID: `git log --all --grep=<id>` and/or the commit messages recorded on the work item comments (implement skill already records commit hashes). The union of files in those commits = touched files.
2. The Key Files section of the work item description (already parsed by `_extract_key_files`).
3. Fallback: if touched-file set cannot be determined (no commits recorded, git unavailable), fail open and re-run the pipeline (current behavior).

**Suggested approach (strict-mode fingerprint):** extend `_compute_content_fingerprint` to a payload of {touched-file set (paths + per-path current git blob hashes or latest commit touching each path), description_hash, key_files} instead of the bare repo HEAD sha. On freshness check, recompute per-path state; equality => fresh. Document trade-offs: the gate is no longer fail-open-cheap the same way, and tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. Unity batch runs rewriting ProjectSettings, see Nova AGENTS.md pitfall #4) must be tolerated — e.g. exclude known tool-artifact paths or accept that they invalidate freshness (safe direction: stale => re-run is never wrong, only wasteful).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] (AC1) Freshness gate decides freshness from the work item touched-file set, not the bare repo HEAD sha: a commit touching only unrelated files does NOT invalidate a stored audit with an unchanged fingerprint
- [ ] (AC2) Any change to a file in the touched-file set invalidates freshness and re-runs the pipeline
- [ ] (AC3) Work-item description/AC/Key Files changes still invalidate freshness (existing behavior preserved)
- [ ] (AC4) Touched-file set resolution falls back to fail-open (re-run pipeline) when it cannot be determined (no recorded commits, git unavailable)
- [ ] (AC5) Tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. ProjectSettings churn from Unity batch runs) are handled explicitly — either excluded from the touched-file comparison or documented as always-invalidating with a test
- [ ] (AC6) Unit tests cover: unrelated-commit freshness (AC1), touched-file change invalidation (AC2), description-change invalidation (AC3), and fail-open fallback (AC4)
- [ ] (AC7) Re-audit of NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U at unchanged state returns the stored verdict without re-running the pipeline (regression scenario from this issue)

## Summary

`audit_runner.py issue|batch --do-not-persist` currently skips **all** persistence, including the `auditedAt` timestamp. A successful dry-run validation (`Ready to close: Yes`) therefore leaves `auditedAt` stale. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:250`) stays `false`, so Herdr's selection list / DOWNTIME audit tier correctly re-queues the item as a stale-audit candidate and shows the ⏳ stale-passed state.

Observed on 2026-09-01 with `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV`: validated with `--do-not-persist --force` (`Ready to close: Yes`, deep analysis completed) but stored audit remained `2026-08-11T05:13:22Z` while `updatedAt` had advanced to `2026-09-01T18:33:14Z` (delta ~21 days via `herdr-downtime` claim + comments). Herdr was correct to show "out of date" — the dry-run never refreshed the freshness signal. Manual `wl audit-set` was required to make `updatedAt == auditedAt` and restore `isAuditFresh: true`.

## Problem

- `--do-not-persist` is documented as a dry run but gives no freshness guarantee; operators assume a passing validation will clear the stale flag, but it does not.
- Help text (`audit_runner.py:10656`, `10781` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) says only "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" — does not explain the Herdr staleness consequence nor the intended dry-run semantics.

## User story

As an operator running `audit_runner.py --do-not-persist` for a dry-run validation, I want a passing validation to still refresh the audit freshness timestamp so Herdr no longer shows the item as out of date, while the full raw report remains not persisted; the flag's help should make this contract explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Freshness on dry-run success:** When `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` (and `batch --do-not-persist` for each drained item) completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item's `auditedAt` is atomically updated to `now` (`updatedAt == auditedAt` in the same txn, `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` pattern) with `auditResult`/`readyToClose` reflecting the verdict, **without** persisting the full `rawOutput` markdown. `isAuditFresh` must be `true` immediately after, and `wl list --stage in_review --json` must show `auditedAt == updatedAt` and `isAuditFresh: true` (Herdr shows ✅ not ⏳ and excludes from audit tier). When the verdict is `Ready to close: No` / `partial` / failure, `auditedAt` is **not** bumped (fail-closed — a failed dry-run must not clear staleness).
2. **Help text updated:** `--do-not-persist` help on both `issue` and `batch` subparsers (and the `SKILL.md` flag table / persistence procedure) is updated to state: dry-run — full audit report is not stored, but on `Ready to close: Yes` the audit freshness timestamp (`auditedAt`/`auditResult`) is still persisted so Herdr/DOWNTIME treat the item as freshly audited; omit the flag to persist the full report. The previous terse "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" is replaced.
3. **No regression for full persist:** Without the flag, behavior is unchanged — full report + `auditedAt`/`auditResult` persisted atomically and lifecycle transitions (`completed`/`in_review` etc.) still apply. With the flag, lifecycle transitions still apply (flag does not suppress status/stage changes).
4. **Tests:** Unit/cli tests cover the new contract: (a) `--do-not-persist` + `Yes` bumps `auditedAt`/`auditResult` but leaves `rawOutput` empty/absent; (b) `--do-not-persist` + `No` does not bump; (c) help text contains the freshness/dry-run wording (mirrors `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` pattern for SKILL.md validation).
5. **Docs:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` persistence section and runner flag docs updated to match the new flag semantics.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` (dry-run left Herdr stale, required manual `wl audit-set` to recover).
- Implementation hint: reuse the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes|no` path (sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in one txn) for the dry-run success case, passing summary but omitting `--raw-output`/`--audit-file` so `rawOutput` stays null. Do not call `wl update --audit-text` afterwards (that would bump `updatedAt` past `auditedAt + 60s` and re-stale).
- `batch` subcommand should apply the same rule per-item in the drain loop.
- Consider whether a new flag (e.g. `--truly-do-not-persist`) is needed for the rare case where even freshness must not be touched; default should be the freshness-preserving dry-run.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` — effort-and-risk SKILL.md output path (the stale-audit observation)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:isAuditFresh` — `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:selectAuditCandidate` / `isAuditFresh` — audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10656,10781` — flag definition
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py:495` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` note
